title: Rav Natan bar Ami
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rava and very wealthy, as in Ketubot 49b, and Bava Batra 8b, where Rava compelled him and took from him four hundred zuz for charity.
And in Shabbat 150b he interpreted it before Rava.
And in Kiddushin 30a Rava said to him, "While your hand is still upon the neck of your son" (marry him off to a wife). And in Bava Batra 135a Rava said to him, "Take it into account."
And in Sanhedrin 30a he said to Ravina, "Thus we say in the name of Rava."

And in Moed Katan 20a it is related that his mother lived in the city of Hozai (far from the city of Mehoza, the place of Rav Natan bar Ami) and died, and he did not hear of it until it had become a distant report; he came before Rava, who ruled for him that he need observe mourning for only one day. He raised an objection against him from a baraita; Rava said to him, "That is an individual opinion, and we do not hold like it."[^1][^2][^3][^4][^5]

notes.text: Hyman reports Rava compelling payment of four hundred zuz for charity; neither the amount nor the coercion is softened.
תרגמא means “he interpreted/explained it.” The entry does not specify the object of that explanation.
The hand-on-the-son’s-neck idiom concerns parental authority; “marry him off” is Hyman’s gloss. חושו לה means taking a matter into account, not concern for an identified woman.

שמועה רחוקה, a “distant report,” is the technical term for news of a death received after the thirty-day period. The one day of mourning is Hyman’s reported ruling. ולא ס״ל כוותיה is read “we do not hold like it,” with ס״ל understood as סבירא לן; it does not negate the death or the obligation to mourn.

The marriage explanation and the distance from Hozai to Mehoza are Hyman’s parenthetical glosses. ב״א is read bar Ami from the heading. The references retain Hyman’s printed folio sides, including Bava Batra 135a.
